stem: What type of pathogen causes Ebola?

options.content: A virus
options.rationale: Correct: the Ebola virus.

options.content: A bacterium
options.rationale: Cholera and typhoid are bacterial; Ebola is viral.

options.content: A single-celled parasite
options.rationale: That is Plasmodium, which causes malaria.

options.content: A fungus
options.rationale: Fungi cause diseases such as ringworm, not Ebola.

explanation: Ebola virus disease is caused by the Ebola virus.

stem: How is Ebola usually spread from one person to another?

options.content: By contact with blood or body fluids of a sick or dead person
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: By the bite of an infected mosquito, like malaria
options.rationale: That is how malaria spreads.

options.content: By drinking water contaminated with faeces, like cholera
options.rationale: That is how cholera mainly spreads.

options.content: By breathing in droplets from the air in the same room
options.rationale: Ebola is not spread through the air.

explanation: Ebola spreads through direct contact, via broken skin or the eyes, nose and mouth, with the blood and body fluids of an infected person or with objects soiled by them.

stem: Ebola can be caught by breathing the same air as an infected person.
explanation: False. Ebola spreads by direct contact with body fluids, not through the air, so gloves, gowns, hand-washing and safe burials can control it.

stem: A person infected with Ebola can spread it to others before any symptoms appear.
explanation: False. People do not spread Ebola before their symptoms begin, which is why tracing contacts and isolating anyone who develops symptoms works.

stem: What is the incubation period of Ebola?

options.content: A few minutes to an hour
options.rationale: Far too short for any infectious disease of this kind.

options.content: 6 to 12 months
options.rationale: Far too long.

options.content: Exactly 7 days
options.rationale: The period varies from person to person.

options.content: 2 to 21 days
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: Symptoms of Ebola appear between 2 and 21 days after infection.

stem: Why are antibiotics not used to cure Ebola?

options.content: Antibiotics are too expensive for treatment centres.
options.rationale: Cost is not the reason: they would not work.

options.content: Ebola patients are allergic to antibiotics.
options.rationale: This is not true.

options.content: Ebola is caused by a virus, and antibiotics do not kill viruses.
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Ebola is caused by a parasite carried by mosquitoes.
options.rationale: Ebola is caused by a virus and is not carried by mosquitoes.

explanation: Antibiotics kill bacteria but have no effect on viruses. Ebola patients receive supportive care and, where available, antibody medicines.

stem: Which of these are early symptoms of Ebola? Select all that apply.

options.content: A swelling in the front of the neck
options.rationale: This is goitre, caused by a lack of iodine.

options.content: Sudden fever
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: A cough lasting more than three weeks
options.rationale: This is a sign of tuberculosis.

options.content: Muscle pain
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Extreme tiredness and weakness
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: A painless sore on the genitals
options.rationale: This is a sign of syphilis.

explanation: Ebola begins suddenly with fever, weakness, muscle pain, headache and sore throat; vomiting, diarrhoea and sometimes bleeding follow.

stem: What name is given to keeping an infected person apart from other people, in a separate ward or treatment centre, so that the disease cannot spread?
explanation: Isolation keeps the patient's body fluids away from family and the community. (Quarantine is the related word for separating healthy contacts who may have been exposed.)

stem: Match each disease with its cause.
explanation: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, typhoid and cholera by bacteria, and Ebola by a virus.

stem: During an Ebola outbreak, trained teams carry out burials instead of families. Why?

options.content: The virus escapes from the soil of the grave and spreads through the air.
options.rationale: Ebola does not spread through the air.

options.content: Trained teams can give the body a vaccine that kills the virus.
options.rationale: Vaccines protect living people; they cannot make a body safe.

options.content: Bodies of Ebola victims carry much virus, so touching them can infect mourners.
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Families might bury the body too close to a borehole and spread the virus in water.
options.rationale: Water is not the main way Ebola spreads; touching the body is.

explanation: Virus levels are very high late in the illness and after death. Washing and touching the body at funerals has spread Ebola, so trained teams with protective clothing carry out safe burials.
hints: Ebola spreads by contact with body fluids. Who touches the body at a traditional funeral?

stem: A health worker checks the temperature of everyone who had contact with an Ebola patient every day for 21 days. Why 21 days?

options.content: The Ebola vaccine takes 21 days to give protection.
options.rationale: That is not the reason for the 21-day check.

options.content: Ebola patients always recover or die within 21 days.
options.rationale: This is not the reason, and many patients survive.

options.content: Fever always appears on exactly the 21st day.
options.rationale: Symptoms can appear on any day from day 2 to day 21.

options.content: 21 days is the longest incubation period for Ebola.
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: The incubation period is 2 to 21 days. Checking contacts for 21 days means anyone who falls ill is isolated at once, and those still well afterwards were not infected.
hints: Link the number to the incubation period of Ebola.

stem: In an area with an Ebola outbreak, which person is at the greatest risk of catching the disease?

options.content: A farmer working alone in fields far from the village
options.rationale: No contact with patients.

options.content: A relative who nurses a sick family member at home without gloves
options.rationale: Correct: they are in direct contact with body fluids.

options.content: A learner who sits in the same bus as a person who has no symptoms
options.rationale: People do not spread Ebola before symptoms begin, and it is not airborne.

options.content: A shopkeeper who sells bread to healthy customers
options.rationale: No contact with body fluids of the sick.

explanation: Caring for the sick without protection brings direct contact with vomit, blood and other body fluids, the main way Ebola spreads.
hints: Which person touches the body fluids of someone who is ill?

stem: Of the four diseases malaria, typhoid, cholera and Ebola, which one is treated first and most urgently with oral rehydration solution (ORS)?

options.content: Malaria
options.rationale: Malaria is treated with antimalarial drugs.

options.content: Cholera
options.rationale: Correct: severe watery diarrhoea dehydrates the patient within hours.

options.content: Typhoid
options.rationale: Typhoid is treated mainly with antibiotics.

options.content: Ebola
options.rationale: Ebola patients also need fluids, but cholera is the disease whose main treatment is immediate ORS.

explanation: Cholera causes sudden, severe watery diarrhoea. Replacing water and salts at once with ORS (or a drip in severe cases) is the most important treatment.
hints: Which disease is best known for causing very rapid dehydration?

stem: An outbreak of Ebola is reported in a neighbouring country, and health workers prepare a treatment centre.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the type of pathogen that causes Ebola.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe two ways in which Ebola is spread from person to person.

points.description: Direct contact with the blood or body fluids (vomit, faeces, urine, saliva, sweat) of a sick or dead person
Contact with objects soiled with body fluids, such as bedding, clothing or used needles; or washing and touching bodies at funerals

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Explain why health workers in the centre wear gloves, gowns and goggles.

points.description: Ebola spreads through body fluids entering broken skin or the eyes, nose and mouth
The clothing stops patients' body fluids reaching the workers' skin and eyes

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State two signs or symptoms of Ebola.

points.description: Sudden fever, or extreme weakness, or muscle pain, or headache, or sore throat
Vomiting, or diarrhoea, or a rash, or bleeding from the gums or nose

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why antibiotics will not cure the patients.

points.description: Antibiotics kill bacteria but Ebola is caused by a virus

explanation: Ebola is a viral disease spread by contact with body fluids. Protective clothing blocks that route, and antibiotics do not act on viruses, so treatment is isolation and supportive care.
hints: Ebola spreads by contact, not through the air.
What kind of pathogen do antibiotics kill?

stem: Malaria, typhoid and Ebola can all begin with a fever, so a clinic must find out which disease a patient has.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the organism that causes malaria.
parts.explanation: Plasmodium (the mosquito is only the vector).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Typhoid and cholera are both spread through contaminated food and water. State one difference between their main symptoms.

points.description: Cholera: sudden, severe watery diarrhoea and vomiting causing rapid dehydration; typhoid: a high fever that rises over several days, with headache, weakness and stomach pain

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: State the main treatment for each of malaria, typhoid and Ebola.

points.description: Ebola: isolation with supportive care (fluids and medicines for fever and pain), or antibody medicines

explanation: The pathogen decides the treatment: antimalarials for Plasmodium, antibiotics for bacteria such as Salmonella Typhi, and supportive care for the Ebola virus.
hints: Match each disease to its pathogen type first: parasite, bacterium or virus.
